leetcode.title: 486. Predict the Winner
leetcode.explanation:
#StreakQ #DP #GameTheory

We play from player 1 perspective and create a DP : dp[left][right] = p1score - p2score

Here left and right are, index of nums array. we use top down approach, to solve this.

The base condition: If left are right are same, we return nums[left]. since its the only value left.

Memo: if dp[left][right] exists, we return it

Now for computation: Take left number : so score willl be nums[left] - recursion(left + 1, right); Here left+1, right, means, p2 will take either from left + 1 or right, so we minus that

Same for right side. Now take max, since we want best for p1. dp[left][right] = max(leftside, rightside) and then we return dp[left][right]

we call this topDown with recursion(0, nums.length-1)

[Leetcode](https://leetcode.com/problems/predict-the-winner/)

leetcode.title: 236. Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
leetcode.explanation:
[236. Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree/description/)

#Neetcode150 [#Tree](https://leetcode.com/problem-list/tree/)

The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in T that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself). 

If the current node is null, return null.

If the current node is p or q, return the current node.

Then recursively search the left and right subtrees.

If both left and right are non-null, it means one target was found in each subtree, so the current node is the LCA. Return root.

Otherwise, if only one side is non-null, return that side (left || right). This propagates the found node (or an already-found LCA) upward.
If both are null, left || right returns null, meaning neither p nor q exists in this subtree.

leetcode.title: 464. Can I Win
leetcode.explanation:
[464. Can I Win](https://leetcode.com/problems/can-i-win/description/) [#GameTheory](https://leetcode.com/problem-list/game-theory/)

In this problem, we do, a running sum, where alice, P1 start by choosing any integer from 1...`maxChoosableInteger` and then Bob, P2 chooses. whoever chooses the last and makes their choice makes the running sum >= `desiredTotal` wins. Note that, you can choose a n integer once, then other player can't choose it, nor you.

So we can use a topDown approach, and think what parameters can explain the situation at any point of the game. 
Its, `active`, the number of active numbers from 0...`maxChoosableInteger ` and `remainingTotal` ie how much `desiredValue` is remaining


so, first we can clear, if its possible to win.
we know running sum from 1..n is (n*(n+1)) / 2

so if n = maxChoosableInteger
then total = (n*(n+1)) / 2
and `if (total < desiredTotal)` then its not a valid game, we can never win, cause the sum isnt even reaching the `desiredTotal`

If it passes, we can play the game.

we will check, 
1) if active numbers are alll used and `remainingTotal > 0`, ie we can't win, return false

2) Now we choose every number from active using loop and see if `number >= remainingTotal`, if yes, we won,  since thats the last number we wanted.

3) Else, Now bob turn, we check `if(!recursion(active.filter(item => item !== i), remainingTotal - i))`

here, i is the currentNumber we are looking at and we simulate if we chose any of the rest of the numbers with remainingTotal - i, since, we already chose current number, we are looking for rest. 

If we its false, that means, BOB couldn't force a win, and next choice Alice may force a win, so we return true

if its true, we bob, will win, so we go for next number in loop

If all the numbers are used, we will get outside the loop, then we loss, so return false


Now since `active` is an array, it will increase timecomplexity, as we are filtering in every loop.

Instead we can use a mask, 
here each bit, will tell, if its active or not
0 -> not used  1 -> used
so we start with 00000

lets say we are trying to use 2
we can check first if 2 integer was already used by 
active & (1 << (i-1))
lets say  active = 00100

now i-1 because bits are indexed from 0
1 << (i-1) => 1 leftShift by 1
ie 00010

now we do AND operation, to see difference
00100 & 00010 = 00000
we get 0 ie its not been used

If it was, we 1 would be at same place, and & operation would give a number


Another instead of doing `active.filter(item => item !== i)`

which is basically removing the current number and creating a new array.

we can do 
`let nextActive = active | 1 << (i-1)`

so if we used 2,
active = 00100
1 << (2-1) => 00010

00100 OR op 00010 => 00110
now we have set the bit as 1, meaning it has been used.

and the best thing is, we can use active as memo, so if in branch, we get to point
we are looking for same active, we can return it using memo
`const memo = new Map()`
`if(memo.has(active)) return memo.get(active)`

leetcode.title: 3310. Remove Methods From Project
leetcode.explanation:
[3310. Remove Methods From Project](https://leetcode.com/problems/remove-methods-from-project/description/)

#StreakQ [#DFS](https://leetcode.com/problem-list/depth-first-search/) [#GraphTheory](https://leetcode.com/problem-list/graph/)

We have given nodes 0..n-1, where n is number of nodes.
and `k` which is the defective/suspecious node number.

A node becomes defective, if there is a directed edge from defective to non-defective

We can remove a group of defective nodes if there are no non-defective nodes edge present or in other ways invoking it.

we have also given `invocations` array, consiting of directed edges eg `[[1,2],[0,1],[3,2]]`
node 1 is connecting to node 2 likewise.

Return an array containing all the remaining methods after removing all the suspicious nodes.

1) Create graph from edges
2) create 2 sets, sus and unsus, which will store the respective nodes
3) DFS from `k` ie defective node until all are visited
4) So we will also need visited array
5) while doing DFS, keep adding them in `sus` set, since we started from defective node, so all are getting defective.
6) Check if `n === sus.size`, ie all nodes are defective, so we will remove everything, hence return []
7) add nodes to `unsus` set which are not present in `sus`
8) now we will check if any of the `sus` nodes are being invoked by an `usus`. if they are being invoked by an `unsus`, we cant remove it.
9)Loop on graph for each node and  neighbours, check for each neighbour `if(unsus.has(node) && sus.has(neighbour))`

ie if `unsus` have a node and that node's neighbour is in `sus`, then we cant remove them

return `[...unsus, ...sus]`

10) else, there are not `unsus` node calling `sus` ones, `return [...unsus]`

leetcode.title: 230. Kth Smallest Element in a BST
leetcode.explanation:
[230. Kth Smallest Element in a BST](https://leetcode.com/problems/kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst/description/)

[#Tree](https://leetcode.com/tag/tree/)
[#Depth-First Search](https://leetcode.com/tag/depth-first-search/)
[#Binary Search Tree](https://leetcode.com/tag/binary-search-tree/)
[#Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/tag/binary-tree/)

we know in BST, left subtree have the smaller value from their parent's value.

In this question, we want Kth smallest value in a BST.

We can use DFS inorder since BST follows inorder left -> root -> right

1) If node is null, return undefined
2) explore left subtree, `let left = dfs(node.left)`
3) `If left !== undefined`, it means the left subtree already found the kth smallest node, so return it immediately.

4) Otherwise, visit the current node : count++
5) If k === count, then we have kth smallest node, so return node's value.
6) Otherwise, explore the right subtree: `return dfs(node.right)`
